War and trade will mix soon enough, and those prepared will profit... or at least survive.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_erebor_9_text}A merchant who sees the storm clouds gathering.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_erebor_9_text}Knowledge of both trade and threats, invaluable combination.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_erebor_9_text}I know every trade route and every threat upon them, information worth its weight in gold.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_erebor_9_text}Merchant-warrior who saw threats others ignored. Now I sell both goods and warnings.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}Honor runs deep in dwarven blood, sometimes deeper than sense...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}I commanded a company of the finest warriors, earned my rank through valor and fairness. My soldiers would follow me into dragon-fire. But honor demanded I speak when I witnessed corruption, a thane skimming from the war supplies, selling weapons meant for our patrols.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}The accusation was true but unprovable, the thane had covered his tracks well. It became my word against his gold and influence. Rather than see me martyred, King Dáin suggested a pilgrimage, a journey to 'seek wisdom.' Exile disguised as honor.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}I accept the king's wisdom but not the corruption it protects. My honor intact, my skills undiminished, I seek those who value truth over politics. The mountain may play its games, but in the wild, integrity and skill matter more than influence.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}Honor preserved through tactical exile, wise solution.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}A commander who values truth over position, rare quality.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}I lead with honor and fight with conviction, qualities that transcend politics.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_erebor_10_text}Honorable captain exiled for exposing corruption. My integrity is unbought and unbroken.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}The mountain's mechanisms are wondrous, but some engineers dream beyond...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}I designed mining equipment, water systems, the great lifts that move between levels. But I also studied war machines, catapults, ballistae, devices mentioned in old texts. Started building prototypes in secret, improvements on ancient designs. Some incorporated... unusual elements.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}They found my workshop during a routine inspection. The flame-throwing ballista scared them most, too reminiscent of dragon-fire, they said. The guild called an emergency meeting, declared my work blasphemous. They gave me three days to leave, my name stricken from the engineer rolls.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}Erebor fears weapons that remind them of past horrors, but our enemies won't hesitate to use fire against us. My designs could save the mountain when war comes. Until they realize this, I'll build for those with clearer vision and fewer haunting memories.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}Innovation deemed blasphemy, fear blinds progress.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}Fighting fire with fire, practical, if disturbing.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}I build weapons others fear to imagine, they'll be grateful when the enemy comes.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_erebor_11_text}Engineer exiled for creating weapons too reminiscent of dragon-fire. Innovation knows no taboos.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}The horses grow restless, and strange wolves prowl our borders...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}I was a Marshal of the Westfold, commanding a éored of riders. We patrolled from Helm's Deep to the Gap of Rohan, watching for threats from Dunland and beyond. But dark rumors came from Isengard.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}My scouts reported strange activity - trees being felled, fires burning day and night, and wolves unlike any we'd seen before. When I brought word to Edoras, Gríma Wormtongue dismissed my concerns, saying Saruman was our ally.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}I pressed the matter, and was relieved of command for 'spreading panic.' Now I ride alone, gathering proof of the threat. The King grows weak under Wormtongue's counsel while danger gathers at our doorstep.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}A watchful eye may save the Mark yet.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}Perhaps you see threats where none exist.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_0_text}I offer my lance and knowledge of these lands, if you need them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}The blood of Eorl runs hot in my veins, demanding action...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}I rode with the cavalry of Aldburg, defending the Eastemnet from orc raids. My spear drank deep of enemy blood, and my horse Thunderfoot was known across the Riddermark for his speed.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}During a skirmish, we pursued orcs too far and discovered they wore gear from Isengard - supposedly our ally. When I reported this to my captain, he ordered me to forget what I'd seen. He said the King's counselor had forbidden such talk.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}I couldn't stay silent while treachery festered. I left my éored and now ride as a masterless warrior, seeking those who still have the courage to face hard truths.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}The Mark needs warriors who won't be silenced.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}Disobedience weakens the realm.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_1_text}My spear and steed are yours, if you'll have them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}Young blood seeks glory, but finds only shadow...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}I earned my first horse at twelve, my first kill at sixteen. I rode with the younger riders of Edoras, eager to prove ourselves worthy of our fathers' legacies. We dreamed of great charges and heroic songs.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}On patrol near the Gap of Rohan, we found burnt villages - not raided by orcs, but destroyed by men. The tracks led toward Isengard. When we reported this, we were told we were mistaken, that Dunlendings were to blame.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}But I know horse tracks from wolf tracks, boot prints from orc spoor. Someone wanted those villages gone, and it wasn't wild men. I left my éored to seek the truth. The Mark is threatened from within and without.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}Youth often sees clearly what age ignores.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}Young eyes can mistake shadows for substance.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_2_text}I offer eager strength and sharp eyes, if you'll have them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}Honor lost is harder to bear than any wound...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}I was thane of a small hall near the Westfold, sworn to Erkenbrand. My people looked to me for protection and justice. I had good riders, strong walls, and fertile lands. It should have been enough.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}Gríma Wormtongue came with tax collectors, demanding twice our usual tribute. When I protested, he accused me of hoarding wealth while the King suffered. He had documents - forged, but convincing - showing I'd traded with Dunland.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}The King, in his befuddled state, stripped me of lands and title. My own people were told I was a traitor. Now I wander, a thane without a hall, seeking to restore my name through deeds since words failed me.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}Wormtongue has destroyed many good men.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}Perhaps there was cause for suspicion.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_3_text}I offer a warrior's skill and bitter experience, if you'll take them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}The shield-maidens of old knew no fear, neither should I...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}My grandmother rode with the éoreds in her youth, before marriage tamed her. She taught me spear and horse in secret, despite my father's wishes. When raiders struck our village while the men were away, I led the defense.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}We held, but I was seen fighting. The village elders said I brought shame, that women who took up arms invited chaos. They demanded I marry immediately or leave. My father, fearing scandal, sided with them.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}I chose exile over chains. Now I ride as my grandmother once did, free and fierce. The Mark needs every spear, regardless of who wields it. Let them whisper - I'll be too busy fighting to hear.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}The Mark wastes half its strength ignoring women warriors.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}Tradition exists for good reasons.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_4_text}I offer a shield-maiden's courage, if you'll accept it.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}The weak die so the strong might live - such is war...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}I rode with the most aggressive éored in the Eastfold. We gave no quarter to orcs, pursuing them to extinction. My commander said mercy to enemies was cruelty to our own people. I believed him.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}We caught a band of Dunlendings rustling cattle. My captain ordered them all killed - men, women, children. I obeyed, but one boy reminded me of my own son. After that night, I couldn't stop seeing his face.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}I left before I lost what humanity remained. Now I fight only those who can fight back. The line between warrior and butcher is thinner than most admit. I've been both, and prefer the former.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}Recognition of evil is the first step to redemption.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}War demands terrible choices.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_5_text}I offer hard skills and harder lessons, if you need them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}The bow sings truest from horseback...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}My father bred horses, my mother was from the Wold where archery is prized. I combined both traditions, becoming one of the few horse archers in the Mark. I could put an arrow through a ring at full gallop.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}Scouting near Isengard, I saw things that shouldn't exist - vast pits, strange fires, and twisted creatures. When I tried to get closer, wolves pursued me - but wolves that ran upright and spoke in dark tongues.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}My captain didn't believe me, said I'd been drinking. Wormtongue heard my tale and declared me mad, suggesting I be confined. I fled that night. What I saw was real, and the Mark must be warned.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}Dark times bring forth dark creatures.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}Fear can make men see monsters.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_6_text}My bow and knowledge are yours, if you'll trust them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}The horses whisper of storms approaching...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}I was born in the saddle, or near enough. My family supplied horses to the King's own stables. I could ride before I could properly walk, and understood horses better than people.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}The horses began refusing to go near the Gap of Rohan - even the bravest stallions would rear and flee. Animals sense evil before men do. When I reported this to the horse masters, they blamed bad training.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}But I know horses. They weren't spooked - they were terrified. Something unnatural grows in Isengard. I left the royal stables to investigate on my own. If the horses fear it, we should too.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}Animals often sense what men miss.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}Horses spook at many things.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_7_text}I offer a rider's skill and a horse's wisdom, if you'll have them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}The finest riders serve truth, not corrupted kings...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}I was chosen for the King's own guard, the elite who ride beside royalty. It was the highest honor a rider could achieve. I served with pride, until I saw how far our King had fallen under Wormtongue's influence.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}Théoden King, once mighty, now sits pale and confused while Wormtongue whispers poison. I heard orders given that made no sense - troops withdrawn from threatened borders, supplies sent to uncertain destinations.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}When I questioned these orders, Wormtongue marked me as 'unreliable.' I was reassigned to distant patrols, then dismissed entirely. I won't serve a puppet king while the real threats gather strength.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}Loyalty to the realm surpasses loyalty to its ruler.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}Abandoning your king seems like treachery.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_8_text}I offer elite training and unwavering purpose, if you need them.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}The plains taught me more than any hall of warriors ever could...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}I grew up in the Eastfold, where the wild horses still run free and the Easterlings probe our borders. My father was a herder, not a soldier, but he taught me to read the land and the wind.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}When raiders came, our village had no éored to protect it. I rallied the young riders and we drove them off ourselves. Word spread, and the Marshal offered me a place in the muster.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}But the marshals quarrel among themselves while the real enemy gathers. I left the muster to find a leader worth following — someone who sees beyond petty border disputes to the true darkness rising in the East.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}A rider who knows the land is worth ten who only know the charge.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}Leaving your people undefended seems reckless.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rohan_9_text}I know every trail and ford in the Riddermark, and my horse has never failed me. That is what I bring.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}Knowledge is the truest weapon, and I have spent a lifetime gathering it...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}I studied the ancient arts of Imladris, learning the secrets of construction and siege-craft from Lord Elrond's own engineers. My family served as builders for generations, raising walls and forging defenses.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}But when a rival accused me of weakening our fortifications for the enemy, I was cast out despite my innocence. The walls I built still stand, though my name has been struck from the builders' rolls.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}Now I wander, offering my knowledge to those who value skill over politics. The Shadow grows, and the Eldar need fortifications more than ever.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}A builder's skills are worth more than a warrior's in these dark times.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}Stone walls won't stop what's coming.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}If you need one who can build as well as fight, I am at your service.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_0_text}A loremaster from Imladris, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}My blade has tasted the blood of many foes, yet I fight on...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}I was a champion of Imladris, trained since youth in the arts of war. My skill with blade and shield earned me renown among the Eldar, and I served Lord Elrond with unwavering loyalty.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}But honor demanded I challenge a corrupt commander who sent soldiers to die for personal glory. I won the duel but lost my position - the commander had powerful allies who saw me banished.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}Now I sell my sword to worthy causes. the forces of darkness grows bolder each day, and there is no shortage of battles to fight for those with the courage to face them.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}A warrior who fights for honor deserves respect.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}Perhaps you should have been more careful about choosing your battles.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}My blade is yours, if you'll have it.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_1_text}A blade-singer from Imladris, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}The wild places hold secrets that town-folk never dream of...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}I served as a scout in Imladris, ranging far beyond our borders to watch for threats. I know every path through the Valley of Rivendell and can track a fox through running water.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}During a patrol, I discovered a plot among our own people - smugglers working with the forces of darkness. When I reported it, I learned the smugglers had bought protection from someone powerful. I was told to forget what I'd seen.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}I refused to look away and paid the price. Now I range alone, using my skills to survive and help those who cross my path. The wilds are dangerous, but at least they're honest.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}The truth is worth any price.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}Sometimes survival requires compromise.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}I offer my eyes, my bow, and my knowledge of the wild.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_2_text}A pathfinder from Imladris, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}I have seen too many die from wounds that could have been healed...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}I trained as a healer in Imladris, learning the properties of every herb and remedy known to the Eldar. I tended the wounded after every skirmish with the forces of darkness, saving countless lives.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}But when a noble's son died despite my best efforts - the wound was beyond any healer's skill - his father blamed me and demanded my execution. I fled rather than face a rigged tribunal.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}Now I practice my art wherever I can, helping the sick and wounded regardless of their allegiance. Death does not discriminate, and neither should healing.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}A healer's compassion is a rare gift.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}Healing enemies only makes more work for warriors.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}If you value the lives of your people, let me tend to them.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_3_text}A healer from Imladris, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}Gold opens doors that swords cannot...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}I built a trading network across Imladris, connecting the Eldar with goods from distant lands. My caravans brought prosperity and rare supplies that Lord Elrond valued highly.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}But a jealous merchant house conspired to frame me for smuggling contraband. They seized my warehouses, scattered my contacts, and left me with nothing but the clothes on my back and the knowledge in my head.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}Now I seek to rebuild, one deal at a time. The coming war will need supplies and logistics, and I know every trade route from the Last Homely House to the far reaches.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}Commerce is the lifeblood of any campaign.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}Pretty words from someone who lost everything.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}I can make your gold stretch further than you'd believe. Hire me.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_4_text}A trader from Imladris, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}In the shadows, one learns the true nature of power...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}I grew up in the back alleys of Imladris, learning to survive by wit and quick hands. Eventually, I was recruited by Lord Elrond's intelligence network, using my skills for the Eldar's benefit.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}But when I uncovered a conspiracy reaching into the highest circles of power, I became a liability. Those I served decided I knew too much and sent assassins. I killed two of them and fled.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}Now I trust no one but myself, though I'd rather use my skills openly than skulk in shadows forever. the forces of darkness has spies everywhere, and someone needs to counter them.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}A shadow-worker who serves the light is valuable indeed.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}How can anyone trust a self-admitted spy?
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rivendell_5_text}I work best when no one sees me coming. Will you have me?

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rhun_6_text}Stripped of rank, I now offer my mind and experience to those who judge by merit, not birth. The coming war will need commanders who can think, not just those who can swing a sword.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rhun_6_text}A thinking warrior is the most dangerous kind.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rhun_6_text}Plans rarely survive contact with the enemy.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rhun_6_text}Let me plan your campaigns, and I'll show you what strategy can achieve.

{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}The ring of hammer on steel is the music I was born to play...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}I was a master smith in the eastern steppes, crafting weapons and armor that the Easterlings prized above all others. My forge produced blades that could cleave through enemy armor like parchment.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}But I refused to craft weapons for a corrupt lord who planned to use them against innocent people. He burned my forge and had me beaten. I survived, but my workshop was destroyed.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}Now I carry my skills wherever I go, maintaining and improving the arms of those I travel with. A good blade in trained hands can change the course of a battle.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}A craftsman of principle is rare and precious.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}Principles don't keep you warm in winter.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}Keep me fed and give me a forge, and I'll keep your steel sharp.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_7_text}A blade smith from the eastern steppes, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}There is no freedom like the wind in your face atop a swift horse...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}I served in the mounted forces of the eastern steppes, patrolling the borders and striking fast against the western kingdoms's raiding parties. My horsemanship was unmatched among the Easterlings.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}During a raid, my commander ordered us to trample fleeing civilians - they might be enemy sympathizers, he said. I refused and was court-martialed for disobedience.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}Now I ride alone, my lance for hire to those who fight with honor. The open road suits me better than garrison duty ever did.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}A rider who values life over orders has true courage.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}Disobedience in battle can cost more lives than it saves.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}Give me a mount and a cause worth riding for.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_8_text}A thunder rider from the eastern steppes, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}An arrow loosed at the right moment can change history...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}I was the finest marksman in the eastern steppes, able to split an arrow at two hundred paces. I served as the Kagan's personal guard archer, watching over the Easterlings from the highest vantage points.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}But I witnessed my captain murder a prisoner in cold blood and reported it. The captain was connected to powerful families, and suddenly I was the one accused of crimes I didn't commit.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}I escaped before they could silence me permanently. Now I offer my bow to those who still believe in justice. Every arrow I loose carries the memory of that murdered prisoner.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}Justice is worth fighting for, even at great cost.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}The dead don't care about justice.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}My bow is steady and my aim is true. Will you have me?
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_rhun_9_text}A storm archer from the eastern steppes, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}Knowledge is the truest weapon, and I have spent a lifetime gathering it...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}I studied the ancient arts of the Haven of Umbar, learning the secrets of construction and siege-craft from the Corsair Lords's own engineers. My family served as builders for generations, raising walls and forging defenses.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}But when a rival accused me of weakening our fortifications for the enemy, I was cast out despite my innocence. The walls I built still stand, though my name has been struck from the builders' rolls.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}Now I wander, offering my knowledge to those who value skill over politics. The Shadow grows, and the Corsairs of Umbar need fortifications more than ever.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}A builder's skills are worth more than a warrior's in these dark times.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}Stone walls won't stop what's coming.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}If you need one who can build as well as fight, I am at your service.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_0_text}A navigator from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}My blade has tasted the blood of many foes, yet I fight on...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}I was a champion of the Haven of Umbar, trained since youth in the arts of war. My skill with blade and shield earned me renown among the Corsairs of Umbar, and I served the Corsair Lords with unwavering loyalty.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}But honor demanded I challenge a corrupt commander who sent soldiers to die for personal glory. I won the duel but lost my position - the commander had powerful allies who saw me banished.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}Now I sell my sword to worthy causes. the navy of Gondor grows bolder each day, and there is no shortage of battles to fight for those with the courage to face them.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}A warrior who fights for honor deserves respect.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}Perhaps you should have been more careful about choosing your battles.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}My blade is yours, if you'll have it.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_1_text}A blade captain from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}The wild places hold secrets that town-folk never dream of...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}I served as a scout in the Haven of Umbar, ranging far beyond our borders to watch for threats. I know every path through the sea fortress and can track a fox through running water.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}During a patrol, I discovered a plot among our own people - smugglers working with the navy of Gondor. When I reported it, I learned the smugglers had bought protection from someone powerful. I was told to forget what I'd seen.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}I refused to look away and paid the price. Now I range alone, using my skills to survive and help those who cross my path. The wilds are dangerous, but at least they're honest.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}The truth is worth any price.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}Sometimes survival requires compromise.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}I offer my eyes, my bow, and my knowledge of the wild.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_2_text}A sea scout from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}I have seen too many die from wounds that could have been healed...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}I trained as a healer in the Haven of Umbar, learning the properties of every herb and remedy known to the Corsairs of Umbar. I tended the wounded after every skirmish with the navy of Gondor, saving countless lives.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}But when a noble's son died despite my best efforts - the wound was beyond any healer's skill - his father blamed me and demanded my execution. I fled rather than face a rigged tribunal.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}Now I practice my art wherever I can, helping the sick and wounded regardless of their allegiance. Death does not discriminate, and neither should healing.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}A healer's compassion is a rare gift.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}Healing enemies only makes more work for warriors.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}If you value the lives of your people, let me tend to them.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_3_text}A ship surgeon from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}Gold opens doors that swords cannot...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}I built a trading network across the Haven of Umbar, connecting the Corsairs of Umbar with goods from distant lands. My caravans brought prosperity and rare supplies that the Corsair Lords valued highly.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}But a jealous merchant house conspired to frame me for smuggling contraband. They seized my warehouses, scattered my contacts, and left me with nothing but the clothes on my back and the knowledge in my head.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}Now I seek to rebuild, one deal at a time. The coming war will need supplies and logistics, and I know every trade route from the corsair docks to the far reaches.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}Commerce is the lifeblood of any campaign.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}Pretty words from someone who lost everything.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}I can make your gold stretch further than you'd believe. Hire me.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_4_text}A prize merchant from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}In the shadows, one learns the true nature of power...

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}I grew up in the back alleys of the Haven of Umbar, learning to survive by wit and quick hands. Eventually, I was recruited by the Corsair Lords's intelligence network, using my skills for the Corsairs of Umbar's benefit.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}But when I uncovered a conspiracy reaching into the highest circles of power, I became a liability. Those I served decided I knew too much and sent assassins. I killed two of them and fled.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}Now I trust no one but myself, though I'd rather use my skills openly than skulk in shadows forever. the navy of Gondor has spies everywhere, and someone needs to counter them.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}A shadow-worker who serves the light is valuable indeed.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}How can anyone trust a self-admitted spy?
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}I work best when no one sees me coming. Will you have me?
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_umbar_5_text}A cutthroat from the Haven of Umbar, seeking purpose and adventure.

{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}The steppe breeds hard riders, and the Ezarkia hardest of all. Ask, and I will tell you how I came to ride alone.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}I led the raiding lances of clan Ezarkia, foremost of the nine tribes of Shaghâna. From the saddle I broke caravans and border forts alike, and brought back more plunder than any rider of my year. The Taskral himself knew my name.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}Then a blood-feud took my cousins, and the elders judged that I had spilled kin to settle it. Whether the charge was true or merely convenient, the oath that bound me to the clan was cut. A rider without a clan is a dead man on the steppe, so I rode west before they could make it so.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}Now my lance answers to coin, and to whoever rides against true enemies. The Taskral musters the tribes for the Dark Lord's war, and there will be plunder enough for any who can take it. I mean to be among them, on my own terms this time.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}A raider cast out by his own blood, but a useful one.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}Ruthless on the steppe, ruthless in my service. I can use that.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}Give me a horse beneath me and an enemy ahead, and you will not find a harder lance for hire.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_0_text}An exiled raid-leader of clan Ezarkia, riding for whoever pays and fights.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}Talk is cheap, and I do not give it away. But for you I will make an exception.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}I kept the tribute-ledgers of clan Kûmaraknis. Every head of cattle, every weight of silver the tribes owed the Taskral passed under my reckoning. I knew to the grain what each fortress could pay, and what it tried to hide.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}A man who counts coin all day learns where coin goes missing, and learns the trick of it himself. When the discrepancy was found, the elders wanted my hands. I left with the contents of one strongbox and the clothes I stood in.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}Coin still loves me and I still love it. I can supply a war-band cheaper than any quartermaster you will hire, skim a little for myself, and you will never feel the loss. The steppe taught me that a full belly beats a clean conscience.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}A thief who keeps good books is still worth his wage.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}He robbed his own clan. He would rob me the moment it paid.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}Put me over your stores and your purse, and both will go further than you think.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_1_text}A disgraced tribute-keeper of clan Kûmaraknis, selling his reckoning to the highest bidder.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}You want the truth of it? Few do. But I have never learned to lie comfortably, so listen.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}I rode in the war-host of clan Taiymâkä and swore the blood-oath young, as we all do. I held it more dearly than most. To me an oath was the only thing on the steppe a man truly owns.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}My captain ordered the lances to ride down a column of unarmed pilgrims on the Taskral's road, to make an example. I would not, and I said why before the whole host. They named me oath-breaker for breaking faith with my captain, never mind the faith I kept with the helpless.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}So I keep my own counsel and my own oath now, and sell my sword only to those who will not make me ashamed to draw it. There is a war coming that will swallow honest men whole. I would rather choose where I spend mine.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}An honest blade is rare. I will take it gladly.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}A man too proud to follow orders is a danger in a fight.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}My oath is yours so long as you keep faith. Break it, and I am gone.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_2_text}An oath-keeper of clan Taiymâkä, exiled for refusing a captain's cruel command.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}I have set more bones than I have broken, which on the steppe is a strange thing to say. Sit, and I will tell you why I wander.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}I was bonesetter and herb-healer to clan Zayaknûri, riding behind the war-host to mend what battle broke. The old women taught me which steppe roots draw fever and which seal a wound, and for many years my hands saved more riders than any lance took.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}But the raids grew crueler as the Taskral bent the tribes to the Dark Lord's purpose. I was made to walk the fields after and finish the enemy wounded rather than tend them. The third time, I could not, and a healer who will not kill is no use to a war-clan.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}Now I go where the hurt are and ask few questions about which banner they bleed under. Hard times are coming for the steppe, and afterward there will be more wounded than healers to meet them. I would be one of the healers.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}A healer is worth ten swords on a long campaign.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}A man who flinches from killing will flinch when I need him.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}Keep me near your wounded and I will keep your riders in the saddle longer than you would believe.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_3_text}A steppe bonesetter of clan Zayaknûri, who left rather than slay the helpless.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}Ha, you have the look of someone with a story of their own. Trade me yours and I will give you mine. No? Then take mine for free.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}I was the best horse-thief clan Selarkes ever raised, which is no small boast among a people who measure a man by the mounts he can take. I could walk into a rival fortress's pens and walk out with their finest stallion, and they would not wake until I was a league gone.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}Trouble is, I never could keep what I took. A good horse to a friend in need, silver to a hungry family, it all ran through my fingers. When I lifted mounts from a clan the Taskral favored and gave them away besides, the elders decided I was more trouble than I was worth.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}So I drift, and there is always need for a man who knows horseflesh and how to acquire it quietly. The tribes are mustering and good mounts will be worth their weight in silver soon. I would rather break and tend them than steal them, if the work is honest enough.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}A man who knows horses is worth keeping close.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}A thief is a thief, however freely he gives it away.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}Trust me with your horses and your road, and neither will let you down.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_4_text}A free-handed horse-thief of clan Selarkes, more at home in the saddle than the law.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}I deal in what men would rather keep hidden. You are certain you want to hear my trade?

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}I was eyes and ears for the lords of clan Uzharês, master of the scouts and the whisperers who watch the steppe forts. I knew which captains took bribes, which oaths were rotten, and which fortress would open its gates before a single arrow flew.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}Knowledge is a blade with two edges. When the clan's lords fell to feuding over the Taskral's favor, I knew too much of all of them to be allowed to live in peace. The losing side named me traitor; the winning side simply wanted me gone before I sold what I knew.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}Now I sell it to whoever pays, and there is no shortage of buyers with a war brewing. Give me a fortress to study and I will tell you how it falls. The Dark Lord's muster has every petty lord watching his neighbor, and a watcher is never out of work.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}Eyes inside the enemy's walls win wars cheaply.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}A spy who betrayed his own lords will betray me as readily.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}Point me at what you must know, and I will bring it back before your enemy knows I looked.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_5_text}A cast-out scout-master of clan Uzharês, trading the steppe's secrets for silver.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}They still tell tales of me at the gathering-grounds, or so I like to think. Here is the truth behind the tales.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}I was the champion of the riding-games of clan Alâranin: the spear-casts, the mounted duels, the contests of nerve the nine tribes hold when they gather. For six summers no rider unseated me, and the Taskral's own captains wagered fortunes on my lance.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}Champions make enemies, and I made mine by keeping every coin I won and lending none of it. When a rival accused me of a foul cast to break my run, the elders sided with the man who shared his winnings more freely. Pride would not let me stay and be doubted.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}So I carry my lance to where it is paid for honestly. The war the Taskral is raising will need men who do not break, and I have never broken at anything. Let others fight for a cause. I fight to be the best, and to be paid like it.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}A proven champion's nerve holds when others fail.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}A man who hoards his winnings will not spend himself for me.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}Wager your battle on my lance and I will not lose you the bet.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_6_text}A games-champion of clan Alâranin, selling his unbeaten lance to the highest bidder.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}An old rider has time for talk, and little else left to him. Sit with me a while.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}For thirty years I was lawspeaker to clan Banûgand, the one who remembered the oaths, judged the feuds, and spoke the old words at the gatherings. The young came to me to settle their quarrels before steel did, and mostly they listened.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}But a blood-feud is older than any lawspeaker, and when it took my own house I could not judge it cold. I ruled against my kin to keep the peace, and my kin never forgave it. An elder without the trust of his clan is only an old man, so I gave up my seat and my hearth.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}Now I offer my counsel to younger captains with wisdom enough to want it. The tribes ride to the Dark Lord's war full of fire and short on memory, and someone must remember what oaths and feuds cost. Perhaps that someone can be of use to you.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}An old head's counsel is worth more than a young arm.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}I need fighters, not an elder past his riding years.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}I am too old to win your battles, but I can keep you from losing them foolishly.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_7_text}A former lawspeaker of clan Banûgand, offering hard-won counsel to those who will hear it.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}I am no great warrior, whatever this scar suggests. But you asked, so I will not hide it.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}I was a herder's son of clan Acammes, happy enough with my goats and the open sky, until the Taskral's muster came through and took every man who could hold a spear. They put me in the war-host and called me a soldier.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}On my first raid we burned a village that had given us no fight: old men, children, all of it, for serving the wrong lord. I had thought we rode to make Shaghâna strong. When I saw what we truly did, I slipped away in the smoke and have not stopped moving since.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}I cannot go home; deserters are made examples of. So I look for a captain who fights men who can fight back, and leaves the helpless alone. I know I am green, but I learn fast, and I will not run from an honest battle. Only from a slaughter.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}An honest heart can be forged into a fine soldier.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}A frightened farm boy who already deserted once? No.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}Take a chance on me and I will repay it. I only ask that the cause be one I can stomach.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_8_text}A conscripted herder of clan Acammes, deserted after a raid he could not bear.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}I make it my business to know things, and to know whom to tell. So, what is it worth to you to know me?

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}I ran goods and men across the steppe borders for clan Shakar: contraband the Taskral taxed too dear, slaves the fortresses wanted quietly, blades to whichever lord paid. I knew every dry wash and hidden well between the tribes and the eastern roads.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}A smuggler survives by selling to all sides and trusting none, and eventually all sides notice. When two clans I had played against each other compared their grievances, the steppe grew too small for me. I took the routes in my head and left the rest behind.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}Now those routes and that knowing are for hire. With the Dark Lord's war coming, armies will need what I can move and the paths I can find. I do not pretend to fight for anyone but myself, and I have found honesty about that serves me better than oaths.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}A man who knows every hidden road is worth his weight.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}He plays all sides. I would be only the next one he sells.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}Need something moved, found, or fetched unseen? That is my trade, and I am the best at it.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_shaghana_9_text}A border smuggler of clan Shakar, selling his hidden roads to whoever pays.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}Every House of Âbanissa is built on its ledgers as much as its spears. I kept one such ledger. Listen.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}I was steward and tax-master to the House of Phaxsharân, one of the great stone dynasties of the southern jungles. The tribute of a dozen villages, the upkeep of the war-beasts, the pay of the House spears, all of it passed through my reckoning, and the House prospered for it.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}A steward who serves too well learns where his masters cheat the Châjaphân's levy, and a steward who knows too much is dangerous when the House falls from favor. When a rival dynasty whispered against us at court, I was the first they cut loose, to prove the House had nothing to hide.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}So I carry my reckoning elsewhere. A war-band is only a small House, and it runs on the same arithmetic: coin in, coin out, and no waste. The Dark Lord's war will ruin the careless and enrich the precise. I intend to be precise, and to serve someone who values it.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}A sharp steward keeps an army fed and paid. Useful.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}A House man who serves whoever pays is cold comfort.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}Set me over your stores and your accounts, and you will campaign longer on less.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_0_text}A cast-off tax-master of the House of Phaxsharân, selling his ledger-craft to a new master.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}I have tended the dying of great Houses. One learns patience, and the worth of plain speech. Ask what you will.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}I was physician to the House of Hoshêdharma, trained in the jungle dynasties' old art of medicine: the fevers of the wetlands, the wounds of beast and blade, the slow poisons the Houses favor against one another. For twenty years I kept the dynasty's blood alive.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}A physician who knows which lord was poisoned, and by whom, holds secrets no House can leave wandering. When my patron died of a sickness I could not prove was natural, his heir wanted no man alive who might have guessed the truth. I was given a purse and a night to be gone.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}Now I tend whoever needs tending and keep a civil tongue. The Châjaphân musters the Houses for the Dark Lord, and war breeds fever and rot as surely as wounds. An army that survives its sicknesses outlasts one that does not. I would see yours outlast its enemies.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}A skilled physician is worth a company of spears.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}A man who fled a poisoning may have brewed it.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}Keep me near your sick and wounded, and fewer of them will go into the ground.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_1_text}A House physician of Hoshêdharma, who fled rather than share a poisoner's secret.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}Stone outlasts the men who raise it. I have raised a great deal of it. Sit, if you would hear how.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}I was master-builder to the House of Vasnârad, raising the stone fortresses that crown the jungles of Âbanissa: walls to break an army, gates no ram could split, cisterns to outlast any siege. The Châjaphân's own strongholds bear my hand.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}A man who knows how a fortress is built knows exactly how it falls, and rival Houses pay dearly for such knowledge. When mine was found to have sold the weak point of a wall, though I will not say I did, the House could not be seen to keep me. Better an old builder exiled than a dynasty disgraced.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}So my craft is for hire, on either side of a wall. With the Dark Lord's war coming, every lord will want his strongholds sound and his enemy's breached. I am too old to climb the ladders, but I can tell you precisely where to set them. Or where to fear them set against you.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}A siege-master turns months of war into days.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}A builder who sold one wall's secret will sell another's.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}Give me your sieges to plan, and walls will cease to be your problem.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_2_text}An exiled siege-builder of the House of Vasnârad, selling the craft of walls and their breaking.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}Discipline, they say, is the soul of an Âbanissan host. I had rather too much of it for my masters' taste. Here is the tale.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}I was a captain of spears for the House of Gorazehan, drilling the dynasty's foot into the disciplined ranks that make our hosts feared. My companies held the line where lesser men broke, and I was proud of every one of them.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}After a battle, the House lord ordered the captured enemy spears put to death rather than ransomed, a waste, and beneath a soldier. I held that a beaten foe who yields is owed his life, and I said so to the lord's face before my men. Discipline, it seems, is only prized when it does not question.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}So I drill other men's companies now, and choose lords who fight like soldiers rather than butchers. The Dark Lord's war will be no gentle thing, I know. But there is a difference between a hard war and a foul one, and I will only lend my craft to the former.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}A disciplined captain is the backbone of any host.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}An officer who defies his lord will defy me too.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}Give me your raw men and a season, and I will give you back soldiers.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_3_text}A House captain of Gorazehan, cast out for sparing prisoners his lord would have slain.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}I am more at home with old scrolls than with swords, but every life turns. Hear mine, if it interests you.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}I was a scribe and lore-keeper in the temple-archives of the House of Azadafrozan, copying the dynasty's histories, its treaties, its rolls of the dead. I know the lineages of every great House of Âbanissa and the old tongues the priests no longer speak.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}I was too free with what I knew. A petitioner came begging the lineage that would prove his claim against a powerful House, and I gave it freely, as I would to anyone, it was only the truth. The House he challenged did not see it so, and the temple could not protect a scribe who had made such an enemy.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}So my learning travels with me now. A captain who can read a captured order, parse a treaty, or know an enemy lord's blood-claims has an edge over one who cannot. The Dark Lord's war is fought with words and lineages as much as spears, and I can fight on that ground at least.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}A lettered man is rare and quietly invaluable.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}A temple clerk is little use in a hard fight.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}I cannot match a soldier's arm, but I can read your enemy better than any of them.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_4_text}A temple scribe of the House of Azadafrozan, exiled for giving away one truth too freely.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}I can be whoever a moment requires. Just now, I am a man telling you the truth, which is rarer for me than you would think.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}I was an agent of the House of Artaxshâsan, the kind a dynasty does not admit to keeping. Forged writs, false seals, a letter in any lord's hand you cared to name, I made the documents that won lawsuits, ruined rivals, and shifted the Châjaphân's favor without a blade ever being drawn.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}A forger's whole life is one good seal away from the executioner. Mine came when a rival House caught a writ I had made and traced the hand to me. My own masters disowned the work the instant it was dangerous, and I had a single night to vanish before the questioners came.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}So my talents are on the market, for those with the stomach to use them. In war, a forged order in the right hands is worth a thousand spears in the wrong place. I do not pretend my trade is honest, but it is effective, and the Dark Lord's war will have ample need of it.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}A forger's cunning can win a war without a battle.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}A man whose whole craft is lies will lie to me first.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}Need a seal forged, a letter placed, an enemy's order turned against him? I am your man.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_5_text}A House forger of Artaxshâsan, fled one step ahead of the questioners, selling his cunning.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}I have spent more years among the great beasts than among men, and trust them further. But I will speak plainly with you.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}I was a beast-master of the House of Ardâcheran, keeper of the war-mûmakil, the towering grey beasts of the southern jungles that no enemy line will stand against. I raised them from calves, knew each by name and temper, and walked beneath their feet without fear.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}A beast is loyal as no man is, and I came to value that loyalty too highly for my masters. When the House drove a tusker to its death in a reckless charge for a lord's glory, and meant to do the same to the rest, I would not lead them to slaughter. A handler who will not spend his beasts is no use to a House that sees them only as engines.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}So I left the beasts I loved rather than watch them die for nothing, and that grief rides with me still. I know warfare and I know command, but I have no taste for throwing lives, beast or man, away for show. Give me a captain who spends his strength wisely, and I will serve him well.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}A beast-master's eye for command is a rare thing indeed.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}A handler with no beasts is just an old soldier now.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}I have no mûmak to bring you, but I bring the judgment that kept them alive. Use it.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_6_text}A war-beast handler of the House of Ardâcheran, who left rather than lead his beasts to slaughter.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}I have made fortunes and lost them, and learned to laugh at both. Pull up a seat for the telling.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}I was master of trade for the House of Tîrdahanâ, a merchant-soldier who kept the dynasty's spears fed, armed, and paid through every campaign. Caravans across the jungle roads, contracts with the coast Houses, the gold that turns a rabble into an army, that was my work, and I was generous in it.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}I backed the wrong claimant. When the House split over which heir should rule, I poured my fortune into the one I judged the better man. He lost. The victor remembered every coin I had spent against him, and a ruined merchant who chose the losing side is welcome in no House of Âbanissa.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}So I rebuild, the only way I know, by making myself useful to someone with a war to fund. The Dark Lord's muster will bankrupt the foolish and enrich the shrewd, and I have learned, expensively, how to tell them apart. Let me keep your army in the field, and I will keep myself in coin.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}A merchant who can supply an army is gold itself.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}A man who gambled away one fortune may gamble mine.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}Trust me with your supply and your trade, and your army will never want for the want of silver.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_7_text}A ruined trade-master of the House of Tîrdahanâ, rebuilding by provisioning other men's wars.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}The jungle hides everything and forgives nothing. I learned to move through it unseen. Listen, and I will tell you how.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}I was a pathfinder for the lesser House of Phaxim, scouting the trackless southern jungles where a wrong turn means a slow death. I could read the wet ground, find the dry path through a swamp, and lead a column where the maps showed only green. The Houses paid well for a man who never lost his way.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}Knowledge of the secret ways is a jealous thing, and my House guarded its routes closely. When I was caught selling a path to a rival, a small thing I thought, and the coin was good, they branded me faithless and turned me out into the very jungle I had mastered. I survived it. Few would have.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}Now my pathfinding is for any captain who needs to go where his enemy does not expect him. War is won by the army that arrives first and unlooked-for, and I can put yours there. The Dark Lord's hosts will march through country that swallows the unprepared. I would see you among the prepared.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}A scout who never loses his way is worth an army's eyes.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}A pathfinder who sold his own House's routes is a risk.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}Send me ahead and your army will never march blind or stray off its road.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_8_text}A jungle pathfinder of House Phaxim, exiled for selling a secret route, now scouting for hire.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}Mine is a short tale and a plain one. I have not lived long enough for a tangled one. Hear it.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}I stood in the household guard of the House of Vashan, sworn to the dynasty's hall and the safety of its lord. It was an honest post for an honest man: to stand watch, to guard the gates, to be the last line between my lord and a blade in the dark.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}My lord was murdered anyway, by his own brother's hand, while I guarded a gate that was never the danger. I would have named the killer before the Châjaphân's court, but the brother sat the high seat now, and a guardsman's word weighs nothing against a House lord's. To stay was to swear loyalty to the man who killed my master. I would not.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}So I carry my sword to where loyalty still means something. I am young, I know, and I have seen one hard year where older men have seen twenty. But I keep my word past breaking, and a captain who can trust the man at his back has something many lords would envy. I would be that man for you.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}Unshakable loyalty in a young sword. I will take it.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}A guardsman who failed his last lord may fail me.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}Give me a post and a lord worth guarding, and I will hold it to the last.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_abanissa_9_text}A young household guardsman of House Vashan, who left rather than serve his master's murderer.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}Quiet. The walls listen under the High Pass, and so do I.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}I was a tunnel-reader for the Great Goblin. I stitched the wounded of the guard with gut and ash, and I knew every passage under the mountain, every crack, every drop of the shaft where we threw the dead, I walked and counted. Nobody else knew how the deep ways joined, so nobody dared to touch me.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}I grew too clever. I sold one back-door passage to a rival chief, only one, for a pit of salt-meat and three slaves. A slave talked. The Great Goblin's boys came for my fingers, and I left through a hole they did not know I had.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}Now I carry the whole mountain in my skull and no lair to put it in. I sell a way in, a way out, a way round, to whoever pays in iron. Never the same way twice.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}A map in the head is worth more than a sword.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}You sold your own tunnels. Why would you not sell me?
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}Give me a warband that pays on time. I will lead it under any mountain you name, and mend the wounded on the way.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_0_text}I mapped the deep ways under the High Pass for Goblin-town. Chiefs pay for a guide who knows the tunnels, so I walk for whoever pays.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}Ha! You look at my scars. Good. Count them.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}The slave pits at the Front Porch had a ring, and I ruled it for four winters. Dwarf captives, men, a Beorning cub once, I broke them all while the crowd screamed. The Great Goblin's own sons put bones on me.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}Then a son of the Great Goblin lost a wager on his pet. They chained my arm to the post and sent in three blades against me. I killed all three and the pet, too. Someone had to pay for that, and it was not him.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}They cast me out through the Front Porch with a rope on my neck. I do not mind. Out here the ring is wherever I stand, and no fat son of a chief chooses who dies in it.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}A champion thrown out for winning. That is an insult.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}You killed the pet and lost your place. Poor judgment.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}Put me in front of your line and watch the others break.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_1_text}I fought in the slave pits under the Front Porch. Pit-fighters who win too often do not last there, so I fight for whoever stands me in front.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}You have a good beast? I had one. Better.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}I raised a warg from a pup in the Great Goblin's kennels. We rode the Vales of Anduin together, burning thatch and dragging off sheep. I kept every coin and every knucklebone from those raids in a hole under my sleeping rock.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}An eagle took him. Out of the clouds, from the eyries above the pass, one stoop, and my warg was torn off the ground in front of me. I ran for two days. When I crept back to the hole, the other whelps had found my hoard and eaten it up like carrion.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}I walk now, and walking is for slaves. I mean to earn another beast, and a bigger hoard, and this time hide it where no thief sniffs. Then I will find the eyrie.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}To lose your beast is a hard thing.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}You hoarded like a dwarf. What did you expect?
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}Pay me and I will ride for you the day you find me a mount.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_2_text}I rode wargs out of the Great Goblin's kennels, raiding the Vales of Anduin. A rider with no beast is worth little, so I hire out and save.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}Captain. Was. Do not salute.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}Eleven years I led the pass raids for the Goblin-town host. Merchants' wagons, dwarf caravans, a Beorning farm if the snow was kind. My plans held. My boys came home fat.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}The last raid, I saw the trap early. Beornings in the trees, both sides. I took the strong ones and ran. The rearguard I left to hold the pass, and they held, and they died. The Great Goblin counted the dead and asked who gave the order.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}So I left before he finished the sum. Honor is a tale for the dead. A plan is what lives, and mine are still good.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}You saved the best of your force. That is sense.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}You left your own to die. Do not expect trust.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}I plan, you pay. If the trap closes, I will not be in it.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_3_text}I led raids on the passes for the Goblin-town host. A captain with a good plan always finds work, and I take it where it pays.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}I watch the high rocks. Birds watch me. Don't speak loud.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}My work was the eyries. I crawled the ledges above the High Pass and counted the great eagles, their nests, their hunts. The chiefs paid in bones and I put aside a little each time.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}A rival clan paid more than the chiefs. Gold-weight of dwarf silver. I sold them the count of the eagles' watch hours, and they struck at dawn and lost half their host to the birds. They knew where it came from. The Great Goblin has my name on his tally-stick.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}I hide in the scree and sell what I see. Nothing in the world stays hid from a scout who does not mind a kick. I only ask who pays last, and who pays most.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}A clever trade, if you live through it.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}You sold your own kin for dwarf silver.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}Take me with you. I see what is behind the next ridge.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_4_text}I watched the passes and the high rocks for Goblin-town. A scout sells what he sees, and I sell it to whoever pays.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}Smell that? Burnt iron. Good. That is my work on me.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}I stood at the Great Goblin's forges and made blades for half the Misty Mountains. Dwarf slaves worked the bellows; I worked the slaves. Every one who lagged got the hot end of the tongs.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}Beornings came down on the forge-gate in a night of snow. Bears the size of ponies. They broke the slave chains and let the dwarves loose, and the dwarves had my own hammers. I killed nine of them with their own steel. The fire took the rest of the forge, and my brothers with it.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}I walked out of the smoke with one hammer and a burnt ear. Now I wander and smash whatever I find, and if there is an anvil on the way I will make you a good blade.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}You paid for that loss in good iron.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}You taught your slaves to hate. They did the rest.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}A host that needs a smith, and does not mind blood on the anvil, I am ready.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_5_text}I worked the forges of the Great Goblin with dwarf slaves at the bellows. A smith always finds an anvil, and I carry my own hammer.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}Bow. Front Porch. Next question.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}I guarded the Front Porch from the shelf above the gate. Anything that came up the road I put an arrow through. Dwarf scouts, tinkers, once a grey-cloaked man with a stick who got away.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}The Great Goblin's tithe-collector took half my kill-share every moon. Said it was the chief's right. One night the share was short. I shot him from the shelf, clean, in the throat, and watched him fall down the steps. Nobody saw. Everybody knew.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}I ran the same night, down to the Vales. Now I shoot for coin from the roadside, or for the pleasure. I have not missed anything bigger than a hare for two winters.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}A fair shot for a fair price.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}You killed your own tithe-man. You will do worse.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}Point me at your enemies and I will thin them before they reach you.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_6_text}I held a bow on the Front Porch for Goblin-town. Anything that comes up the road, I shoot, and I will do it for coin anywhere.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}Oh, you want a story? I have one. It ends badly. Mine all do.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}I raided the Vales of Anduin since I had teeth, and when the host wanted a gate broken I built the rams and ladders for it. Cattle, children's toys, the odd Beorning's roof. The pack laughed at my jokes and followed me anywhere. Then the shaman threw her bones for me.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}She said I would die under the shadow of wings, and would be last of the pack. So the pack stopped sleeping next to me. One by one they took other captains, and I walked alone at the back, grinning, since there was nothing else to do with my mouth.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}I am still alive, which is a poor omen for the bones. If you are the wings, make it quick. If you are not, give me a spear and I will stand in front of you and make the shaman a liar.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}Doom is only a word the weak whisper.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}A cursed one. I will keep my back to the wall.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}Bones lie as often as I do. Let me fight under your banner.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_7_text}I raided the Vales of Anduin and built the ladders and rams for the pass assaults. Goblins talk of omens; I say the work is the work.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}You look at my face. Good. Look at my hands as well.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}I held a place in the Great Goblin's own guard, a post for whoever could crack a skull and not be missed. My company kept the throne-cave and the hot stair. We were thirty. We were the best the tunnels grew.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}A dwarf-hunt went down the old shaft and I led it. They knew the walls better than we did. Their axes came out of the dark, and the shaft took twenty-six of mine. The Great Goblin said the fault was the leader's. I was the leader.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}He gave me a night to be gone. I took two knives and the helm of the last of my dead. Now I look for a hall where nobody asks who lost the shaft, and a dwarf to pay the debt.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}No blame on a leader who survived a trap.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}Twenty-six dead. I would have hanged you.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}I need a war to feed and a dwarf to kill. I am yours until I have both.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_8_text}I served the Great Goblin's guard in the tunnels and hunted dwarves in the old shafts. A spear-arm is always wanted, so I carry mine.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}A fine day for a trade. Is it not? Is it always?

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}The slave pits were mine, in a way. I kept the tally, the chains, the price of a dwarf, of a Rohirric farm-girl, of a Beorning cub. The Great Goblin paid me a tenth. He is generous, as spiders are.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}I shaved the count. Not much, a head in twenty, sold on the side to a trader of Rhovanion. A new overseer counted again. One head short, then two, then eleven. I will say only that I am grateful for a long throwing arm and a short corridor.
{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}I have kept my coin and lost my place. I still know every buyer from the Vales to the Anduin ford. Anything can be sold, including you, though not today.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}Cheating the Great Goblin takes spine.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}A thief who robs his own chief. How comforting.
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}Hire me to plan your battles. I can make any field and any tally agree with you.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_goblin_9_text}I worked the slave pits and the tallies of Goblin-town. Anything can be bought or sold there, and a battle is just another count.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}Every corpse has a number. Ask me what yours is worth.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}At Mount Gram I mended the chieftain's wounded and kept the tally-bones. Every skull from the last great defeat went on my strings, ours and theirs, and I knew who lived and who was owed. Nobody counts the counter.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}A pale rider from the south paid in silver for my numbers: how many Bolg's sons had left, where the holds stood thin. I sold him all of it. Then a rival read my strings, found the gaps, and counted me among the dead.

{=aom_backstory_c.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}I walked out through a drain before they came to count properly. Now I sell my numbers to whoever bleeds silver, and I keep one string for every warband that has crossed me.
{=aom_response_1.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}A careful mind is worth more than a loud one.
{=aom_response_2.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}You sold your own hold. Why should I be spared the same?
{=aom_backstory_d.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}Pay me fair and I will count your enemies for you, and keep your name off my strings.
{=aom_generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_0_text}Mount Gram and the northern holds always need someone to mend the wounded and keep the tally of the dead. That is my trade.
{=aom_prebackstory.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_1_text}Say the word Carrock to me. Go on. See what I do.

{=aom_backstory_a.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_1_text}I was the first through every door in my warband. My axe was three paces of reach and I never counted heads, only skulls. The hold sang of me, and I believed the song.

{=aom_backstory_b.spc_wanderer_mistymountainorcs_1_text}We went up to the Carrock after a Beorning. I ran at him alone, and he was not a man but a bear the size of a wagon. The warband stood on the rocks and watched. He broke my shoulder and my pride, and not one of them came down.
